Project.Name: non-person-identity.xml
Project.Title: Non-Person Identity Modernization: Service Accounts, Workload Identities and AI Agents

Task.Name: Phase 0 — Inventory
N0.1 AD service accounts discovered, read-only: traditional accounts, MSAs, gMSAs and dMSAs, classified by type and risk with a suggested target
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/b02-identity/09-building-the-entra-target.md#discovering-service-accounts

Task.Name: X-G0 Program G0 — Ready to Plan: the read-only assessment committed
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Steward (program) If decided late: The program's assessment goes to G0 without the service account picture, and Phase 1 is sized without it Source: program-master-schedule.md

Task.Name: X-A03 App registrations, owners, credentials and granted permissions inventoried (Privileged Access plan, A0.3)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering (Privileged Access plan) If decided late: The Entra side of the register has no app registration inventory to start from Source: privileged-access.md

Task.Name: N0.2 Entra workload identities added to that inventory: managed identities, federated credentials, consent grants; ownerless and secret-holding apps flagged
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/b04-access/05-applications-and-workload-identities.md#a-read-only-inventory-to-start-from

Task.Name: N0.3 AI seed list: the current AI use-case inventory vintage loaded; agentic, purchased and no-ATO entries matched to agent identities and service principals
Task.Contact: Identity engineering, with the Chief AI Officer's staff
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering, with the Chief AI Officer's staff Source: ../books/b17-ai-identity/03-the-inventory-as-an-identity-source.md#using-the-inventory-as-the-seed-list

Task.Name: N0.4 SQL Server engine, login and LDAP-bind accounts tagged and handed to the Data Platform plan
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/b06-data-platform/09-what-arc-provides-to-sql-server.md#the-managed-identity-and-the-service-account

Task.Name: N0.5 One non-person identity register: type, host, workload location, risk and candidate target for every identity
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#non-person-identity-track

Task.Name: D-N1 Source of record for non-person identities
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: CIO Options: The owning workload's record (the system inventory or CMDB entry and the application registration) and, for AI, the AI use-case inventory, with the register keyed to them; a separate identity register kept by the identity team If decided late: The register has nothing to reconcile against, and owners and lifecycle have nothing to hang from Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#non-person-identity-track

Task.Name: NG0 Gate 0 — Non-person identities inventoried
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: ISSO Criteria: Every AD service account, MSA, gMSA and dMSA, every app registration, service principal and managed identity, and every AI use case in the current vintage in one register with type, risk and candidate target; HIGH-risk accounts listed; stale leads confirmed against sign-in logs, not retired on a guess; SQL Server accounts handed to the Data Platform plan Source: ../books/b02-identity/10-migrating-and-governing.md#phase-4-service-account-modernization

Task.Name: Phase 1 — Ownership
N1.1 An application owner found for every service account; two human owners on every app registration and service principal; serviceManagementReference set
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Application owners Source: ../books/b04-access/05-applications-and-workload-identities.md#ownership

Task.Name: N1.2 AI accountability: a federal sponsor mastered in HR, a small sponsoring group, a technical owner who isn't the sponsor, and a matching inventory record
Task.Contact: Sponsoring offices, with the identity governance officer
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Sponsoring offices, with the identity governance officer Source: ../books/b17-ai-identity/05-owners-sponsors-and-lifecycle.md#the-programs-rule-two-named-humans-and-a-record

Task.Name: D-N2 Orphan rule for identities nobody will own
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: CISO Options: Disable once the identity governance officer confirms the finding, then 30 days for the office to name an owner or retire it (Book 04's rule, applied at once to agents because they can act); retire at once; keep running on a dated exception If decided late: Unowned accounts can't be disposed of, and Gate 1 can't pass Source: ../books/b04-access/06-who-decides-access.md#ownership-changes-and-orphaned-apps

Task.Name: N1.3 Unowned identities disabled, not deleted, under the orphan rule; each a retirement candidate with a 30-day claim window
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity governance officer Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#service-accounts-msas-gmsas-and-dmsas

Task.Name: NG1 Gate 1 — Every non-person identity owned
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: CISO Criteria: Every service account has a named application owner; every app registration and service principal has two human owners and a service-management reference; every AI identity has a federal sponsor, a sponsoring group, a technical owner and a matching inventory record; every unowned identity is disabled pending retirement or carries a dated exception Source: ../books/b02-identity/09-building-the-entra-target.md#governing-service-principals

Task.Name: Phase 2 — Decide per account
N2.1 Target set per account from the migration path matrix: app registration, managed identity, gMSA or dMSA, or retirement
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering, with application owners Source: ../books/b02-identity/09-building-the-entra-target.md#the-migration-path-matrix

Task.Name: D-N3 Retire, re-platform or keep, account by account
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Application owners Options: Retire (unused or unowned); re-platform to a managed identity, a gMSA or dMSA, or an app registration with a federated credential or certificate; keep on Kerberos with an SPN, islanded with an end date the authorizing official accepts If decided late: The conversion waves can't be built, and the program's SPN retirement (P4.6) has no list to work from Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#non-person-identity-track

Task.Name: D-N4 Workload ID Premium licensing scope
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: CISO Options: License for the single-tenant service principals classified Tier 1 (Book 04's position); license more widely; don't license, and rely on app management policies and owner reviews, with no workload Conditional Access If decided late: Workload Conditional Access can't be created or changed, and privileged service principal reviews aren't available Source: ../books/b04-access/05-applications-and-workload-identities.md#what-workload-id-premium-adds

Task.Name: N2.2 Conversion waves sequenced: HIGH-risk accounts first (password never expires, over-privileged); rollback recorded per wave
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/b02-identity/10-migrating-and-governing.md#phase-4-service-account-modernization

Task.Name: NG2 Gate 2 — Every account has a decision
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: ISSO Criteria: Every account in the register has a disposition (retire, re-platform, or keep with an end date) and a target from the matrix; HIGH-risk accounts in the first wave; every kept Kerberos account has an SPN owner; waves and their rollback recorded Source: ../books/b02-identity/10-migrating-and-governing.md#phase-4-service-account-modernization

Task.Name: Phase 3 — Credential modernization
X-G1 Program G1 — Foundation Complete: groups and AUs drift-clean, Conditional Access baseline enforced
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Steward (program) If decided late: Conversion has no group and policy foundation to land on (Book 02 puts service accounts after group migration) Source: program-master-schedule.md

Task.Name: N3.1 App management policy: new client secrets and symmetric keys blocked, certificates capped at 180 days for new apps; app instance property lock on owned apps
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/b04-access/05-applications-and-workload-identities.md#enforcing-the-order-with-app-management-policies

Task.Name: N3.2 Wave 1, HIGH-risk accounts: workload identities created (managed identity, then federated credential, then certificate); federated token exchange tested
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering, with application owners Source: ../books/b02-identity/09-building-the-entra-target.md#workload-identity-federation

Task.Name: N3.3 Wave 1 parallel run: old and new credentials side by side for 30 days, then the legacy accounts disabled
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Application owners Source: ../books/b02-identity/10-migrating-and-governing.md#phase-4-service-account-modernization

Task.Name: N3.4 Remaining waves converted, each with its own 30-day parallel run before the legacy account is disabled
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering, with application owners Source: ../books/b02-identity/10-migrating-and-governing.md#phase-4-service-account-modernization

Task.Name: N3.5 Kerberos-only workloads: MSAs upgraded to gMSAs; traditional accounts, IIS application pools and scheduled tasks moved to a gMSA or a dMSA
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Server infrastructure Source: ../books/b02-identity/09-building-the-entra-target.md#the-migration-path-matrix

Task.Name: X-D08 End dates for legacy authentication and NTLM (program D08)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Authorizing official (program) If decided late: Kerberos accounts that stay can't be given end dates, so the islanded list can't be handed to the program Source: program-master-schedule.md

Task.Name: N3.6 Kerberos accounts that stay: SPN owner and an end date within D08 recorded; the islanded list handed to the program's SPN retirement
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/b02-identity/10-migrating-and-governing.md#what-still-needs-ad-after-phase-10

Task.Name: N3.7 Rotation in place: certificates in Key Vault, rotated by the pipeline, raised before expiry and approved by the owner
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/b04-access/05-applications-and-workload-identities.md#governing-app-registrations

Task.Name: NG3 Gate 3 — Credentials modernized
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: ISSO Criteria: Every HIGH-risk account converted or retired; no account with a password that never expires; new identities authenticate without stored secrets where the host allows, otherwise with a certificate on the rotation schedule; no client secret in production outside a dated exception; legacy accounts disabled after a clean 30-day parallel run with no service disruption; every remaining Kerberos account islanded with an owner and end date Source: ../books/b02-identity/10-migrating-and-governing.md#phase-4-service-account-modernization

Task.Name: X-DG4 SQL Server's application chain on Entra principals (Data Platform plan, Gate 4)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: ISSO (Data Platform plan) If decided late: The SQL Server accounts handed over in Phase 0 are still on Windows authentication Source: data-platform.md

Task.Name: X-P46 AD-bound service principal names migrated, retired or islanded (program P4.6)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Application owners (program) If decided late: The program measures AD authentication for G4 while converted workloads still hold AD credentials Source: program-master-schedule.md

Task.Name: Phase 4 — Least privilege
N4.1 Permission sweep: owners review every grant; broad permissions such as Directory.ReadWrite.All replaced with application-specific roles and scopes
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Application owners Source: ../books/b02-identity/09-building-the-entra-target.md#governing-service-principals

Task.Name: N4.2 Managed identities' role assignments scoped to the resource and put on the app registrations' review cadence
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/b04-access/05-applications-and-workload-identities.md#managed-identities

Task.Name: X-A34 Non-human privileged identities owned, off secrets, over-consented apps swept (Privileged Access plan, A3.4)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity governance officer (Privileged Access plan) If decided late: Privileged service principals are outside this plan's sweep, so the least-privilege gate can't pass Source: privileged-access.md

Task.Name: N4.3 First quarterly owner review of permissions closed; access reviews for service principals in privileged roles
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity governance officer Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#service-principals-managed-identities-and-workload-identities

Task.Name: NG4 Gate 4 — Least privilege
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: CISO Criteria: No service principal holds a broad tenant-wide permission without a recorded justification; managed identities' role assignments scoped to resources; privileged non-human identities closed in the Privileged Access plan; the first quarterly review cycle closed with its findings acted on Source: ../books/b02-identity/09-building-the-entra-target.md#governing-service-principals

Task.Name: Phase 5 — Conditional Access for workload identities
N5.1 Scope set: Tier 1 single-tenant service principals assigned directly, never through a group; workload egress ranges named; managed identities and multitenant apps recorded as out of scope
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/b02-identity/09-building-the-entra-target.md#conditional-access-for-workload-identities

Task.Name: N5.2 CA015 location restriction and CA037 high-risk block in report-only; service principal sign-in logs read
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/b04-access/07-the-conditional-access-policy-library.md#wave-4-risk-and-workload-identities

Task.Name: D-N5 Enforce the workload identity policies
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: CISO Options: Enforce; extend report-only; enforce with named exclusions, each recorded with its owner and end date If decided late: Tier 1 workloads stay reachable from anywhere with a stolen credential, and Gate 5 can't pass Source: ../books/b04-access/05-applications-and-workload-identities.md#conditional-access-for-workload-identities

Task.Name: N5.3 Policies enforced ring by ring; block events alerted to security operations
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/b04-access/07-the-conditional-access-policy-library.md#wave-4-risk-and-workload-identities

Task.Name: NG5 Gate 5 — Workload identities under Conditional Access
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: CISO Criteria: Every Tier 1 single-tenant service principal assigned directly to the enforced location and risk policies; report-only results reviewed before enforcement; every out-of-scope identity (managed identities, multitenant and SaaS apps) recorded with the control that covers it instead Source: ../books/b04-access/05-applications-and-workload-identities.md#conditional-access-for-workload-identities

Task.Name: Phase 6 — AI agents
D-N6 AI identity capabilities the program builds on in the agency's cloud
Task.Contact: CIO, with the Chief AI Officer
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: CIO, with the Chief AI Officer Options: Agent identities where generally available in the agency's cloud, with GCC's documented subset; service principals and managed identities under the same governance where agent identities aren't available; preview capabilities as watch items If decided late: Agents are created with no decided identity type, and the production handshake can't be defined Source: ../books/b17-ai-identity/04-kinds-of-ai-identity.md#release-stage-licensing-and-government-clouds

Task.Name: N6.1 Creation closed: Users can create agent blueprints set to No; agent app registrations routed to the blueprint path; consent baseline applied to agents
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/b17-ai-identity/06-credentials-and-least-privilege.md#admin-consent-and-the-scuba-consent-baseline

Task.Name: N6.2 Production handshake: blueprint, sponsor, consent, Conditional Access coverage and placement confirmed; access through expiring access packages
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/b17-ai-identity/05-owners-sponsors-and-lifecycle.md#creation

Task.Name: N6.3 Agent credentials: managed identity as the blueprint credential, else federation, else a certificate; no secret on a production blueprint
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering, with technical owners Source: ../books/b17-ai-identity/06-credentials-and-least-privilege.md#no-stored-secrets

Task.Name: N6.4 Agent least privilege: access mode chosen first; narrow inheritance, never allAllowed for app roles; no standing privileged role
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/b17-ai-identity/06-credentials-and-least-privilege.md#privileged-roles-for-ai-none-standing

Task.Name: X-IG4 Mover and leaver automation proven (Identity Lifecycle plan, Gate 4)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: ISSO (Identity Lifecycle plan) If decided late: The sponsor's mover and leaver events have no HR-driven workflow to ride on Source: identity-lifecycle.md

Task.Name: N6.5 Sponsorship tasks added to the HR-driven mover and leaver workflows; ten-business-day confirmation; human workflows kept off agents' user accounts
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/b17-ai-identity/05-owners-sponsors-and-lifecycle.md#when-the-sponsor-moves-or-leaves

Task.Name: N6.6 Agent Conditional Access in report-only: block all agent identities except those approved by attribute; block high-risk agents (preview, watch item)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/b17-ai-identity/06-credentials-and-least-privilege.md#the-token-subject-decides-which-policy-applies

Task.Name: N6.7 AI drift checks running: agentic system with no governed identity, shadow AI identity, no accountable human, credential added outside the pipeline
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Security operations Source: ../books/b17-ai-identity/07-monitoring-drift-and-shadow-ai.md#drift-comparing-what-was-declared-with-what-is-observed

Task.Name: NG6 Gate 6 — AI identities governed
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: CISO Criteria: Every AI system in the current inventory vintage classified by kind of identity; every agent identity created through the handshake with a sponsor, a technical owner and a matching inventory record; no production blueprint with a client secret; no AI identity with a standing privileged role; sponsor mover and leaver tasks live; agent block policies in report-only with results reviewed; no open P1 AI drift finding Source: ../books/b17-ai-identity/10-evidence-and-authorization.md#the-evidence-an-authorizing-official-needs

Task.Name: Phase 7 — Steady state
N7.1 Register drift scheduled: ownerless, unused or expiring registrations, passwords that never expire, credentials added outside the pipeline
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/b02-identity/10-migrating-and-governing.md#git-based-drift-detection

Task.Name: N7.2 A full review cycle: owners' quarterly permission review, sponsors' attestation, expiry-based recertification of agent access
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity governance officer Source: ../books/b17-ai-identity/05-owners-sponsors-and-lifecycle.md#recertification-expiry-is-the-review

Task.Name: X-D11 Provisional target end state: AD retired, or a dated Kerberos island (program D11)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Executive sponsor and CIO (program) If decided late: The gMSA and dMSA reconciliation has no target to reconcile against Source: program-master-schedule.md

Task.Name: N7.3 gMSAs and dMSAs reconciled with the provisional end state: moved to a workload identity, or listed for the Kerberos island with an end-of-life date
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#service-accounts-msas-gmsas-and-dmsas

Task.Name: X-G5 Program G5 — AD Retired
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Executive sponsor and CIO (program) If decided late: A workload still running under a gMSA loses its credential when the last domain controller is demoted Source: program-master-schedule.md

Task.Name: N7.4 Evidence to the ISSO for AC-2, AC-6(5), IA-4, IA-5 and IA-9, and for M-25-21; the annual inventory vintage comparison scheduled
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity governance officer Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#federal-requirements

Task.Name: NG7 Gate 7 — Steady state
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: ISSO Criteria: Every service account and service principal has an owner and sponsor, a reason and a target; each is retired, re-platformed to a managed identity or gMSA, or a certificate or federated workload identity; none holds a password that never expires and none is orphaned; drift checks and review cycles running; every remaining gMSA and dMSA moved or in the dated Kerberos island Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#non-person-identity-track
